title.zh: 卷一百二十三 志第七十六 禮二十六
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 志第七十六 禮二十六 Volume 123 Treatises 76: Rites 26

sentences.zh: 園陵濮安懿王園廟秀安僖王園廟莊文景獻二太子欑所上陵忌日

translations.literal: Garden tombs; garden temples of Prince Pu Anyi the Tranquil and Respectful and Prince Xiu Anxi the Happy and Joyful; memorial days for imperial tombs compiled and submitted by the two crown princes Zhuangwen and Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial garden tombs; the garden temples of Princes Pu Anyi and Xiu Anxi; and tomb memorial days submitted in memorial by Crown Princes Zhuangwen and Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 皇后園陵。

translations.literal: Garden tombs of empresses.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses' imperial garden tombs.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年六月二日，皇太后杜氏崩於滋德殿。

translations.literal: On the second day of the sixth month in the second year of Jianlong of Taizu, Empress Dowager née Du died at Zide Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the sixth month in the second year of Jianlong, Empress Dowager Du, mother of the dynasty, died at Zide Hall.

sentences.zh: 三日，百官入臨。

translations.literal: On the third day, the hundred officials entered to offer condolence.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day, all officials came to pay their respects at the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 明日大斂，欑于滋福宮，百官成服，中書、門下、文武百僚、諸軍副兵馬使以上並服布斜巾四腳、直領襽衫，外命婦帕頭、帔、裙衫。

translations.literal: The next day the great encoffinement; she was placed in the coffin at Zifu Palace; the hundred officials assumed full mourning; Secretariat, Chancellery, civil and military officials, and deputy military commissioners and above all wore cloth mourning caps with four corners and straight-collared ramie shirts with inner collars; women of rank outside the palace wore kerchiefs, shawls, and skirt-robes.
translations.idiomatic: The next day came the great encoffinement, and she was laid in the coffin palace at Zifu Palace. Officials of every rank assumed full mourning dress: members of the Secretariat and Chancellery, civil and military officers, and military commissioners and above all wore four-cornered cloth mourning caps and straight-collared ramie mourning shirts; women of rank outside the palace wore kerchiefs, shawls, and skirt-robes.

sentences.zh: 九日，帝見百官於紫宸門。

translations.literal: On the ninth day, the Emperor received the hundred officials at the Zichen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day the Emperor received the officials at the Zichen Gate.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「皇后、燕國長公主高氏、皇弟泰甯軍節度使光義、嘉州防禦使光美並服齊衰三年。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "The Empress, Princess Chang of Yan the elder née Gao, the Emperor's younger brother Guangyi, military commissioner of Taining, and Guangmei, defender of Jiazhou, should all wear second-grade mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Rites reported: "The Empress, Princess Chang of Yan the elder, Lady Gao, the Emperor's brother Guangyi, military commissioner of Taining, and Guangmei, defender of Jiazhou, should all observe three years of second-grade mourning.

sentences.zh: 准故事，合隨皇帝以日易月之制，二十五日釋服，二十七日禫除畢，服吉，心喪終制。」

translations.literal: According to precedent, they should follow the Emperor in the system of substituting days for months; on the twenty-fifth day they should end mourning dress; on the twenty-seventh day the chan removal should be complete and they should wear auspicious dress, with inner mourning until the full term ended."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent they were to follow the Emperor's rule of substituting days for months: on the twenty-fifth day they would lay aside mourning garments, on the twenty-seventh day complete the chan removal and wear auspicious dress, while inner mourning continued to the end of the full term."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，太常禮院言：「准詔議定皇太后諡，按唐憲宗母王太后崩，有司集議，以諡狀讀於太廟，然後上之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Directorate of Rites said: "Per the edict to deliberate the posthumous title of the Empress Dowager—when Wang, mother of Emperor Xianzong of Tang, died, the relevant offices convened to deliberate and read the posthumous title document in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, then presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Directorate of Rites reported: "By edict we are to deliberate the Empress Dowager's posthumous title. When Wang, mother of Emperor Xianzong of Tang, died, the relevant offices met in council, read the posthumous title document in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and only then presented it upward.

sentences.zh: 周宣懿皇后諡，即有司撰定奏聞，未常集議，制下之日，亦不告郊廟，修諡冊畢始告廟，還，讀於靈坐前。」

translations.literal: When the posthumous title of Empress Xuanyi of Zhou was conferred, the relevant offices drafted and reported it; they did not customarily convene for deliberation; on the day the order was issued they did not announce it at the suburban altars or ancestral temple; only after the posthumous book was completed did they announce it at the temple, and upon returning read it before the spirit seat."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xuanyi of Zhou received her posthumous title, the relevant offices drafted it and reported upward without the usual council; on the day the order was issued they did not announce it at the suburban altars or the ancestral temple. Only after the posthumous book was finished did they announce it at the temple, and on returning read it before the spirit seat."

sentences.zh: 詔從周制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the Zhou precedent be followed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the Zhou precedent be followed.

sentences.zh: 於是，太常少卿馮吉請上尊諡曰明憲皇太后。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Director Feng Ji of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested the elevated posthumous title Illustrious and Discerning Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Feng Ji requested the elevated posthumous title Illustrious and Discerning Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 九月六日，群臣奉冊寶告於太廟，翌日上于滋福宮。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the ninth month, the multitude of officials presented the book and seal and announced them at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the next day they were presented at Zifu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the ninth month the officials presented the book and seal and announced them at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the next day they were presented at Zifu Palace.

sentences.zh: 十月十六日，葬安陵。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the tenth month, she was buried at An Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the tenth month she was buried at An Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十一月四日，神主祔太廟宣祖室。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the eleventh month, her spirit tablet was enshrined in the chamber of Imperial Ancestor Xuan in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the eleventh month her spirit tablet was enshrined in the chamber of Imperial Ancestor Xuan in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，改卜安陵于河南府鞏縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, An Mausoleum was relocated by divination to Gong County in Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, An Mausoleum was relocated by divination to Gong County in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月二十五日，奉寶冊，改上尊諡曰昭憲皇太后，讀于陵次。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the third month, the precious book was presented; the elevated posthumous title was changed to Illustrious and Commiserating Empress Dowager, read at the mausoleum site.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the third month the precious book was presented and the elevated posthumous title was changed to Illustrious and Commiserating Empress Dowager, read at the mausoleum site.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，啟故安陵。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day, the former An Mausoleum was opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day the former An Mausoleum was opened.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，靈駕發引，命攝太尉、開封尹光義遣奠，讀哀冊。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day the spirit procession set out; Guangyi, acting Grandee of Ceremonies and acting prefect of Kaifeng, was ordered to conduct the farewell offering and read the lamentation book.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day the spirit procession set out. Guangyi, acting as Grandee of Ceremonies and prefect of Kaifeng, was ordered to conduct the farewell offering and read the lamentation book.

sentences.zh: 四月九日，掩皇堂。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the fourth month, the imperial crypt was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the fourth month the imperial crypt was sealed.

sentences.zh: 太祖孝明、孝惠二後。

translations.literal: The two empresses Xiaoming and Xiaohui of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The two empresses Xiaoming and Xiaohui of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年十二月七日，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the twelfth month in the first year of Qiande, Empress née Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the twelfth month in the first year of Qiande, Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，命樞密承旨王仁贍為園陵使。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day, Privy Council administrative aide Wang Renzan was appointed commissioner for the garden mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day Privy Council administrative aide Wang Renzan was appointed commissioner for the garden mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 時議改卜安陵于鞏，並以二後陪葬焉。

translations.literal: At the time it was debated to relocate An Mausoleum by divination to Gong, and the two empresses were to be buried beside it as companions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated relocating An Mausoleum by divination to Gong, with the two empresses to be buried there as companion tombs.

sentences.zh: 皇堂之制，下深四十五尺，上高三十尺。

translations.literal: Regulations for the imperial crypt: depth below forty-five chi, height above thirty chi.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial crypt was to be forty-five chi deep below and thirty chi high above.

sentences.zh: 陵台再成，四面各長七十五尺。

translations.literal: The mausoleum platform was in two tiers; each of the four sides measured seventy-five chi.
translations.idiomatic: The mausoleum platform was built in two tiers, each side seventy-five chi long.

sentences.zh: 神牆高七尺五寸，四面各長六十五步。

translations.literal: The spirit wall was seven chi five cun high; each of the four sides was sixty-five paces long.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit wall was seven chi and five cun high, each side sixty-five paces long.

sentences.zh: 南神門至乳台四十五步，高二丈三尺。

translations.literal: From the southern spirit gate to the nursing platform was forty-five paces; the platform was two zhang three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: From the southern spirit gate to the nursing platform was forty-five paces; the platform stood two zhang and three chi high.

sentences.zh: 吉仗用中宮鹵簿，凶仗名物悉如安陵而差減其數，孝惠又減孝明焉。

translations.literal: Auspicious regalia used the inner palace insignia; funeral regalia names and items all followed An Mausoleum but with reduced numbers; Xiaohui's was further reduced from Xiaoming's.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious regalia followed the inner palace insignia; funeral regalia in name and kind all followed An Mausoleum but in reduced numbers, and Xiaohui's was further reduced below Xiaoming's.

sentences.zh: 二年三月二十七日，孝明皇后啟欑宮，群臣服初喪之服；

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the third month in the second year, Empress Xiaoming's coffin palace was opened; the multitude of officials wore initial mourning dress;
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day of the third month in the second year, Empress Xiaoming's coffin palace was opened and the officials wore initial mourning dress;

sentences.zh: 明日，孝惠皇后自幄殿發引。

translations.literal: the next day, Empress Xiaohui's spirit procession set out from the curtained hall.
translations.idiomatic: the next day Empress Xiaohui's spirit procession set out from the curtained hall.

sentences.zh: 皆設遣奠，讀哀冊。

translations.literal: Both had farewell offerings set out and the lamentation book read.
translations.idiomatic: For both, farewell offerings were set out and the lamentation book was read.

sentences.zh: 四月九日，葬孝惠于安陵之西北，孝明于安陵之北。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the fourth month, Xiaohui was buried northwest of An Mausoleum and Xiaoming north of An Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the fourth month Xiaohui was buried northwest of An Mausoleum and Xiaoming to its north.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，皆祔於別廟。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day, both were enshrined in the separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day both were enshrined in the separate temple.

sentences.zh: 其後，孝明升祔太祖室。

translations.literal: Later, Xiaoming was elevated to enshrinement in Taizu's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaoming was elevated to enshrinement in Taizu's chamber.

sentences.zh: 太宗賢妃李氏，真宗至道三年十二月追尊為皇太后，諡曰元德，祔葬永熙陵。

translations.literal: Consort Xian of Taizong, née Li—in the twelfth month of the third year of Zhidao of Zhenzong she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager, posthumous title Primordial Virtue, and buried beside Yongxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xian of Taizong, Lady Li—in the twelfth month of the third year of Zhidao, Zhenzong posthumously honored her as Empress Dowager with the title Primordial Virtue and buried her beside Yongxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，升祔太宗室。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, she was elevated to enshrinement in Taizong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu she was elevated to enshrinement in Taizong's chamber.

sentences.zh: 太宗明德皇后李氏，真宗景德元年三月十五日崩。

translations.literal: Empress Mingde of Taizong, née Li—on the fifteenth day of the third month in the first year of Jingde of Zhenzong she died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mingde of Taizong, Lady Li—died on the fifteenth day of the third month in the first year of Jingde.

sentences.zh: 十七日，群臣上表請聽政，凡五上始允。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day, the multitude of officials submitted memorials requesting that he hear government; only after five submissions did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day the officials submitted memorials asking him to resume government; only after five submissions did he consent.

sentences.zh: 帝去杖、絰，服衰，即御坐，哀動左右。

translations.literal: The Emperor removed staff and headband, wore second-grade mourning, and immediately took the imperial seat; his grief moved those on either side.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laid aside staff and mourning headband, put on second-grade mourning dress, and took the throne at once; his grief moved all who stood beside him.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「皇后宜准昭憲皇太后禮例，合隨皇帝以日易月之制。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Rites said: "The Empress should follow the ritual precedent of Illustrious and Commiserating Empress Dowager and follow the Emperor in the system of substituting days for months.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Rites reported: "The Empress should follow the precedent set for Illustrious and Commiserating Empress Dowager and observe the Emperor's rule of substituting days for months.

sentences.zh: 宗室雍王以下，禫除畢，吉服，心喪終制。」

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen from Prince Yong down—when the chan removal was complete they wore auspicious dress, with inner mourning until the full term ended."
translations.idiomatic: For imperial clansmen from Prince Yong downward, when the chan removal was complete they wore auspicious dress while inner mourning continued to the end of the full term."

sentences.zh: 五月，詳定園陵，宜在元德皇太后陵西安葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the garden mausoleum was determined in detail; she should be buried west of Primordial Virtue Empress Dowager's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the garden mausoleum was fixed in detail: she was to be buried west of Primordial Virtue Empress Dowager's tomb.

sentences.zh: 八月十二日，上諡。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the eighth month, the posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the eighth month her posthumous title was conferred.

sentences.zh: 九月二十二日，遷坐于沙台欑宮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the ninth month, the spirit seat was moved to the coffin palace at Shatai.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the ninth month the spirit seat was moved to the coffin palace at Shatai.

sentences.zh: 十月七日，祔神主太宗室。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the tenth month, her spirit tablet was enshrined in Taizong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the tenth month her spirit tablet was enshrined in Taizong's chamber.

sentences.zh: 三年十月十五日，帝詣欑宮致奠。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the tenth month in the third year, the Emperor went to the coffin palace to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the tenth month in the third year the Emperor went to the coffin palace to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 十六日，發引。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day, the spirit procession set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day the spirit procession set out.

sentences.zh: 二十九日，掩皇堂。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day, the imperial crypt was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day the imperial crypt was sealed.

sentences.zh: 真宗章穆皇后郭氏，景德四年四月十五日崩。

translations.literal: Empress Zhangmu of Zhenzong, née Guo—on the fifteenth day of the fourth month in the fourth year of Jingde she died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangmu of Zhenzong, Lady Guo—died on the fifteenth day of the fourth month in the fourth year of Jingde.

sentences.zh: 皇帝七日釋服，後改用十三日。

translations.literal: The Emperor ended mourning dress on the seventh day; later this was changed to the thirteenth day.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laid aside mourning on the seventh day; later the period was changed to thirteen days.

sentences.zh: 群臣三日釋服。

translations.literal: The multitude of officials ended mourning dress on the third day.
translations.idiomatic: The officials laid aside mourning on the third day.

sentences.zh: 諸道、州、府官吏訃到日舉哀成服，三日而除。

translations.literal: Officials of circuits, prefectures, and districts—on the day the death notice arrived they raised lamentation and assumed mourning dress, ending on the third day.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of every circuit, prefecture, and district, on the day the death notice arrived, raised lamentation and assumed mourning dress, laying it aside after three days.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，司天監詳定園陵。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day, the Directorate of Astronomy determined the garden mausoleum in detail.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day the Directorate of Astronomy fixed the garden mausoleum in detail.

sentences.zh: 帝令祔元德皇太后陵側，但可安厝，不必寬廣，其棺槨等事，無得鐫刻花樣，務令堅固。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered burial beside Primordial Virtue Empress Dowager's tomb; it need only provide a resting place, without need for breadth; as to coffin and inner coffin, no carved floral patterns—they must be made solid.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered her buried beside Primordial Virtue Empress Dowager's tomb with only a modest resting place, not a spacious layout. Coffin and inner coffin were not to bear carved floral patterns but were to be made solid and strong.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，殯于萬安宮之西階。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day, she was laid in state on the western steps of Wanan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day she was laid in state on the western steps of Wanan Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔兩制、三館、秘閣各撰挽詞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Hanlin academicians, the Three Institutes, and the Secret Repository each to compose dirges.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Hanlin academicians, the Three Institutes, and the Secret Repository each to compose dirges.

sentences.zh: 閏五月十三日，上諡曰莊穆。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the intercalary fifth month, the posthumous title Dignified and Solemn was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the intercalary fifth month she received the posthumous title Dignified and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 六月二十一日，葬永熙陵之西北。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the sixth month, she was buried northwest of Yongxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the sixth month she was buried northwest of Yongxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 七月，有司奉神主謁太廟，祔享于昭憲皇后，享畢，祔別廟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the relevant offices presented the spirit tablet to visit the Imperial Ancestral Temple, enshrined for offering with Illustrious and Commiserating Empress; when the offering was complete, enshrined in the separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the relevant offices brought the spirit tablet to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, enshrined her for joint offering with Illustrious and Commiserating Empress, and after the rites enshrined her in the separate temple.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年四月十五日，大祥。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month in the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the great auspicious mourning rite was held.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month in the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu came the great auspicious mourning rite.

sentences.zh: 詔特廢朝，群臣奉慰。

translations.literal: An edict specially suspended court; the multitude of officials presented condolences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially suspended court, and the officials presented condolences.

sentences.zh: 真宗宸妃李氏，仁宗明道元年二月二十六日薨。

translations.literal: Consort Chen of Zhenzong, née Li—on the twenty-sixth day of the second month in the first year of Mingdao of Renzong she died.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Chen of Zhenzong, Lady Li—died on the twenty-sixth day of the second month in the first year of Mingdao.

sentences.zh: 初葬洪福禪院之西北，命晏殊撰墓銘。

translations.literal: She was first buried northwest of Hongfu Chan Monastery; Yan Shu was ordered to compose the tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: She was first buried northwest of Hongfu Chan Monastery, and Yan Shu was ordered to compose the tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 二年四月六日，追冊為莊懿皇太后。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the fourth month in the second year, she was posthumously enregistered as Dignified and Commiserating Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the fourth month in the second year she was posthumously enregistered as Dignified and Commiserating Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 十月五日，改葬永定陵之西北隅。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the tenth month, she was reburied in the northwest corner of Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the tenth month she was reburied in the northwest corner of Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十七日，祔神主於奉慈廟。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day, her spirit tablet was enshrined in Fengci Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day her spirit tablet was enshrined in Fengci Temple.

sentences.zh: 真宗章獻明肅皇后劉氏，明道二年三月二十七日崩於寶慈殿，遷坐於皇儀殿。

translations.literal: Empress Zhangxian Mingsu of Zhenzong, née Liu—on the twenty-seventh day of the third month in the second year of Mingdao she died at Baoci Hall; the spirit seat was moved to Huangyi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangxian Mingsu of Zhenzong, Lady Liu—died on the twenty-seventh day of the third month in the second year of Mingdao at Baoci Hall, and her spirit seat was moved to Huangyi Hall.

sentences.zh: 三十日，宣遺誥，群臣哭臨，見帝於殿之東廂奉慰。

translations.literal: On the thirtieth day, the testamentary edict was proclaimed; the multitude of officials wept in condolence and saw the Emperor in the eastern wing of the hall to present condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirtieth day the testamentary edict was proclaimed. The officials wept in condolence and received the Emperor in the eastern wing of the hall to present condolences.

sentences.zh: 宗室削杖不散發。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen shaved the staff but did not loosen the hair.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen shaved the mourning staff but did not loosen their hair.

sentences.zh: 中書、樞密、使相比宗室，去斜巾、垂帽、首絰及杖。

translations.literal: Compared with imperial clansmen, Secretariat and Chancellery, Privy Council, and commissioners removed slanting caps, hanging caps, headbands, and staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with imperial clansmen, members of the Secretariat and Chancellery, the Privy Council, and commissioners removed slanting caps, hanging caps, headbands, and staffs.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士至龍圖閣直學士已上、並節度使、文武二品已上，又去中單及褲。

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians through associate academicians of the Dragon Diagram Hall and above, together with military commissioners and civil and military officials of the second rank and above, also removed inner skirts and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin academicians through associate academicians of the Dragon Diagram Hall and above, together with military commissioners and civil and military officials of the second rank and above, also removed inner skirts and trousers.

sentences.zh: 兩省、御史台中丞文武百官以下，四腳幅巾、連裳、腰絰。

translations.literal: Officials of the two secretariats, censors-in-chief of the Censorate, and civil and military officials below wore four-cornered kerchiefs, linked robes, and waist bands.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the two secretariats, censors-in-chief of the Censorate, and all civil and military officials below wore four-cornered kerchiefs, linked robes, and waist mourning bands.

sentences.zh: 館閣讀書、翰林待詔、伎術官並給孝服。

translations.literal: Readers in the institutes, Hanlin awaiting edicts, and technical officers were all issued mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Readers in the institutes, Hanlin awaiting edicts, and technical officers were all issued mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 宰相、百官朝晡臨三日，內外命婦朝臨三日。

translations.literal: Chancellors and the hundred officials attended morning and evening condolence for three days; women of rank inside and outside the palace attended morning condolence for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors and all officials attended morning and evening condolence for three days; women of rank inside and outside the palace attended morning condolence for three days.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣使告哀遼、夏及賜遺留物。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning to Liao and Xia and to bestow bequest goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Liao and Xia and to bestow bequest goods.

sentences.zh: 十日，司天監詳定山陵制度。

translations.literal: On the tenth day, the Directorate of Astronomy determined the mountain mausoleum regulations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day the Directorate of Astronomy fixed the mountain mausoleum regulations in detail.

sentences.zh: 皇堂深五十七尺。

translations.literal: The imperial crypt was fifty-seven chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial crypt was fifty-seven chi deep.

sentences.zh: 神牆高七尺五寸，四面各長六十五步。

translations.literal: The spirit wall was seven chi five cun high; each of the four sides was sixty-five paces long.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit wall was seven chi and five cun high, each side sixty-five paces long.

sentences.zh: 乳台高一丈九尺，至南神門四十五步。

translations.literal: The nursing platform was one zhang nine chi high; from it to the southern spirit gate was forty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: The nursing platform stood one zhang and nine chi high, forty-five paces from the southern spirit gate.

sentences.zh: 鵲台高二丈三尺，至乳台四十五步。

translations.literal: The magpie platform was two zhang three chi high; from it to the nursing platform was forty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: The magpie platform stood two zhang and three chi high, forty-five paces from the nursing platform.

sentences.zh: 詔下宮更不修蓋，餘依。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the lower palace not be rebuilt or roofed; the rest followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the lower palace not be rebuilt or roofed; the rest followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，以宰臣張士遜為山園使。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, Chancellor Zhang Shixun was appointed commissioner for the mountain garden.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day Chancellor Zhang Shixun was appointed commissioner for the mountain garden.

sentences.zh: 是日，翰林學士馮元請上尊諡；

translations.literal: That day, Hanlin academician Feng Yuan requested the elevated posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: That day Hanlin academician Feng Yuan requested the elevated posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 九月四日，讀於靈坐。

translations.literal: on the fourth day of the ninth month it was read at the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: on the fourth day of the ninth month it was read at the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 十月五日，葬永定陵之西北隅。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the tenth month, she was buried in the northwest corner of Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the tenth month she was buried in the northwest corner of Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十七日，祔神主於奉慈廟。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day, her spirit tablet was enshrined in Fengci Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day her spirit tablet was enshrined in Fengci Temple.

sentences.zh: 真宗章惠皇后楊氏。

translations.literal: Empress Zhanghui of Zhenzong, née Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhanghui of Zhenzong, Lady Yang.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年十一月五日，保慶皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Jingyou, Baoqing Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Jingyou, Baoqing Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「皇帝本服緦麻三月，皇帝、皇后服皆用細布，宗室皆素服、吉帶，大長公主以下亦素服，並常服入內，就次易服，三日而除。」

translations.literal: The Directorate of Rites said: "The Emperor in his own person wears fourth-grade mourning for three months; the Emperor and Empress both use fine cloth dress; imperial clansmen all wear plain dress with auspicious belts; princesses of the great eldest rank and below also wear plain dress; all enter in ordinary dress and change dress at their stations, ending on the third day."
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Rites reported: "In his own person the Emperor owes three months of fourth-grade mourning. The Emperor and Empress are both to wear fine cloth. Imperial clansmen are to wear plain dress with auspicious belts, and princesses of the great eldest rank and below likewise plain dress. All are to enter in ordinary dress and change at their stations, laying mourning aside after three days."

sentences.zh: 詔以「保祐沖人，加服為小功，五日而除。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "In protecting the young sovereign, mourning is increased to third grade, ending after five days."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "In protecting the young sovereign, mourning is increased to third grade and laid aside after five days."

sentences.zh: 四年正月十六日，上諡。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the first month in the fourth year, the posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the first month in the fourth year her posthumous title was conferred.

sentences.zh: 二月六日，葬永定陵之西北隅。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the second month, she was buried in the northwest corner of Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the second month she was buried in the northwest corner of Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十六日，升祔奉慈廟。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day, she was elevated to enshrinement in Fengci Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day she was elevated to enshrinement in Fengci Temple.

sentences.zh: 仁宗慈聖光獻皇后曹氏。

translations.literal: Empress Cisheng Guangxian of Renzong, née Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Cisheng Guangxian of Renzong, Lady Cao.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐二年十月二十日，太皇太后崩于慶壽宮。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the tenth month in the second year of Yuanfeng of Shenzong, the Grand Empress Dowager died at Qingshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the tenth month in the second year of Yuanfeng, the Grand Empress Dowager died at Qingshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，文武百官入宮，宰臣王珪升西階，宣遺誥已，內外舉哭，盡哀而出。

translations.literal: That day, civil and military officials entered the palace; Chancellor Wang Gui ascended the western steps; when the testamentary edict had been proclaimed, those inside and outside raised lamentation, exhausted their grief, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That day civil and military officials entered the palace. Chancellor Wang Gui ascended the western steps, and when the testamentary edict had been proclaimed, those inside and outside raised lamentation, exhausted their grief, and departed.

sentences.zh: 二十六日大斂，命韓縝為山陵按行使。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day the great encoffinement was held; Han Zhen was appointed commissioner for inspection of the mountain mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day came the great encoffinement, and Han Zhen was appointed commissioner for inspection of the mountain mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 二十九日，皇帝成服。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day, the Emperor assumed full mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day the Emperor assumed full mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 十一月，韓縝言：「永昭陵北稍西地二百十步內，取方六十五步，可為山陵。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Han Zhen said: "Within two hundred ten paces slightly west of Yongzhao Mausoleum's north, taking a square of sixty-five paces, it can serve as the mountain mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Han Zhen reported: "Within two hundred ten paces slightly west of the north side of Yongzhao Mausoleum, a square plot of sixty-five paces on each side can serve as the mountain mausoleum."

sentences.zh: 上以迫隘，縝言：「若增十步，合征火相主及中五之數。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said it was cramped; Han Zhen said: "If increased by ten paces, it would match the numbers governing the Fire phase lord and the central five."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said the site was too cramped. Han Zhen replied: "If we add ten paces, it will accord with the numbers governing the Fire phase and the central five."

sentences.zh: 詔增十步。

translations.literal: An edict ordered an increase of ten paces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the plot increased by ten paces.

sentences.zh: 十二月，中書言：「先是，司天監選年月，遷祔濮安懿王三夫人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Secretariat said: "Previously, the Directorate of Astronomy selected the year and month for relocating and enshrining the three consorts of Prince Pu Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Secretariat reported: "Earlier the Directorate of Astronomy had selected the year and month for relocating and enshrining the three consorts of Prince Pu Anyi.

sentences.zh: 今大行太皇太后山陵，濮三夫人亦當舉葬。」

translations.literal: Now for the mountain mausoleum of the late Grand Empress Dowager, the three consorts of Pu should also be interred."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the late Grand Empress Dowager's mountain mausoleum is at hand, the three consorts of Pu must also be buried."

sentences.zh: 於是詔宗室正任防禦使以上許從靈駕，已從濮安王夫人者，免從。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict allowed imperial clansmen holding regular posts of defender and above to follow the spirit procession; those who had already followed Prince Pu Anyi's consorts were excused.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict allowed imperial clansmen holding regular posts of defender and above to follow the spirit procession, while those who had already followed Prince Pu Anyi's consorts were excused.

sentences.zh: 三年正月十四日，上諡。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the first month in the third year, the posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the first month in the third year her posthumous title was conferred.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「大行太皇太后雖已有諡，然山陵未畢，俟掩皇堂，去'大行'，稱慈聖光獻太皇太后；

translations.literal: The Directorate of Rites said: "Although the late Grand Empress Dowager already has a posthumous title, as the mountain mausoleum is not yet complete, when the imperial crypt is sealed, remove 'late' and call her Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian;
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Rites reported: "Although the late Grand Empress Dowager already has a posthumous title, the mountain mausoleum is not yet finished. When the imperial crypt is sealed, remove 'late' and style her Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian;

sentences.zh: 祔廟題神主，仍去二'太'字。」

translations.literal: when enshrining in the temple, inscribe the spirit tablet, still removing the two characters 'Grand.'"
translations.idiomatic: when enshrining her in the temple, inscribe the spirit tablet but still omit the two characters 'Grand.'"

sentences.zh: 秘閣校理何洵直言：「按禮，既葬，日中還，虞於正寢。

translations.literal: Associate collator He Xunzhi of the Secret Repository said frankly: "According to the rites, after burial, at midday return and perform yu at the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Associate collator He Xunzhi of the Secret Repository submitted a frank memorial: "According to the rites, once burial is complete one returns at midday and performs the yu offering at the main chamber.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者之葬，近在國城之北，故可以平旦而往，至日中即虞於寢，所謂葬日虞，弗忍一日離也。

translations.literal: In antiquity burial was near the north of the capital, so one could go at dawn and by midday perform yu at the chamber—the so-called yu on the burial day, unable to bear separation even for a day.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the dead were buried just north of the capital, so mourners could set out at dawn and by midday perform the yu at the main chamber—the 'yu on the burial day,' unwilling to be parted even for a single day.

sentences.zh: 後世之葬，其地既遠，則禮有不能盡如古者。

translations.literal: Later burials were far away, so the rites could not fully follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages burial grounds lay far away, so the rites could no longer be observed exactly as in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今大行太皇太后葬日至第六虞，自當行之於外，如舊儀；

translations.literal: Now from the burial day of the late Grand Empress Dowager to the sixth yu, they should be performed outside as in old custom;
translations.idiomatic: For the late Grand Empress Dowager, from the burial day through the sixth yu, the rites should be performed outside the palace as in former custom;

sentences.zh: 其七虞及九虞、卒哭，謂宜行之于慶壽殿。

translations.literal: the seventh yu, ninth yu, and final wailing—I submit should be performed at Qingshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: the seventh yu, the ninth yu, and the final wailing should, I submit, be performed at Qingshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 又按《春秋公羊傳》曰： '虞主用桑。

translations.literal: Also according to the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals: 'Yu spirit tablets use mulberry.'
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals also says: 'Yu spirit tablets are made of mulberry.'

sentences.zh: '《士虞禮》曰：'桑主不文。

translations.literal: The Rites of Yu for Officers says: 'Mulberry tablets are unadorned.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Yu for Officers says: 'Mulberry tablets are left unadorned.'

sentences.zh: '伏請罷題虞主。」

translations.literal: I respectfully request that inscribing yu tablets be discontinued."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully ask that the court discontinue inscribing posthumous titles on yu tablets."

sentences.zh: 太常言：「洵直所引，乃士及諸侯之禮。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "What Xunzhi cited is the rite for officers and feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices replied: "What Xunzhi cited applies to officers and feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 況嘉祐、治平並虞于集英殿，宜如故事。

translations.literal: Moreover in Jiayou and Zhiping they all performed yu at Jiying Hall—should follow precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the Jiayou and Zhiping reigns the yu rites were all performed at Jiying Hall, and precedent should be followed.

sentences.zh: 又嘉祐、治平，虞主已不書諡，當依所請。」

translations.literal: Also in Jiayou and Zhiping, yu tablets did not inscribe posthumous titles—should follow the request."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou and Zhiping as well, yu tablets did not bear posthumous titles; the request should be granted."

sentences.zh: 太常禮院又言：「慈聖光獻皇后祔廟，前三日，告天地、社稷、太廟、皇后廟如故事。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Rites also said: "For Empress Cisheng Guangxian's enshrinement in the temple, three days before, announce to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Empresses' temple as in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Rites also reported: "Three days before Empress Cisheng Guangxian is enshrined in the temple, announcements should be made to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Empresses' temple, following precedent.

sentences.zh: 至日，奉神主先詣僖祖室，次翼祖、宣祖、太祖、太祖後。

translations.literal: On the day, present the spirit tablet first to Imperial Ancestor Xi's chamber, then Yi's, Xuan's, Taizu's, and Taizu's consorts.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the spirit tablet should be presented first to Imperial Ancestor Xi's chamber, then to those of Yi, Xuan, Taizu, and Taizu's consorts.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝、懿德皇后、明德皇后同一祝，次饗元德皇后。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, Empress Yide, and Empress Mingde share one prayer; next offer to Empress Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, Empress Yide, and Empress Mingde share one prayer text; next offer to Empress Yuande.

sentences.zh: 慈聖光獻皇后，異饌、異祝，行祔廟之禮。

translations.literal: Empress Cisheng Guangxian—separate offerings, separate prayer—perform the enshrinement rite.
translations.idiomatic: For Empress Cisheng Guangxian, with separate offerings and a separate prayer, perform the enshrinement rite.

sentences.zh: 次真宗、仁宗、英宗室。

translations.literal: Next the chambers of Zhenzong, Renzong, and Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Next visit the chambers of Zhenzong, Renzong, and Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，奉神主歸仁宗室。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the spirit tablet was returned to Renzong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the spirit tablet was returned to Renzong's chamber.

sentences.zh: 如此，則古者祔謁之禮及近代遍饗故事，並行不廢。」

translations.literal: Thus the ancient rite of enshrinement visitation and the recent custom of offerings at every chamber would both be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: In this way both the ancient rite of enshrinement visitation and the recent custom of offerings at every chamber would be preserved."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 三月十日，葬永昭陵。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the third month, she was buried at Yongzhao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the third month she was buried at Yongzhao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，祔於太廟。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day, she was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day she was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 英宗宣仁聖烈皇后高氏，哲宗元祐八年九月三日崩于崇慶宮。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren Shengle of Yingzong, née Gao—on the third day of the ninth month in the eighth year of Yuanyou of Zhezong she died at Chongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren Shengle of Yingzong, Lady Gao—died on the third day of the ninth month in the eighth year of Yuanyou at Chongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 遺誥：「皇帝成服，三日內聽政，群臣十三日，諸州長吏以下三日而除。

translations.literal: Testamentary edict: "The Emperor assumes full mourning; within three days he hears government; the multitude of officials thirteen days; prefectural chief administrators and below end on the third day.
translations.idiomatic: Her testamentary edict read: "The Emperor is to assume full mourning and resume government within three days; officials for thirteen days; prefectural chief administrators and below for three days.

sentences.zh: 釋服之後，勿禁作樂。

translations.literal: After laying aside mourning dress, do not forbid music.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning dress is laid aside, music is not to be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 園陵制度，務遵儉省。

translations.literal: Garden mausoleum regulations—strive to follow frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Garden mausoleum arrangements are to be kept frugal.

sentences.zh: 余並如章獻明肅皇太后故事。」

translations.literal: The rest all follow the precedent of Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu."
translations.idiomatic: All else follows the precedent of Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu."

sentences.zh: 十四日，詔園陵依慈聖光獻太皇太后之制。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day, an edict ordered the garden mausoleum to follow the regulations of Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day an edict ordered the garden mausoleum to follow the regulations established for Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年正月二十八日，禮部言：「將題神主，謹按章獻明肅皇后神主書姓劉氏。」

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the first month in the first year of Shaosheng, the Ministry of Rites said: "When inscribing the spirit tablet, we respectfully note that Empress Zhangxian Mingsu's spirit tablet bears the surname Liu."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the first month in the first year of Shaosheng the Ministry of Rites reported: "When the spirit tablet is inscribed, precedent shows that Empress Zhangxian Mingsu's tablet bore the surname Liu."

sentences.zh: 詔依故事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that precedent be followed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that precedent be followed.

sentences.zh: 四月一日，葬永厚陵。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, she was buried at Yonghou Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month she was buried at Yonghou Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 神宗欽聖憲肅皇后向氏，建中靖國元年正月十三日崩。

translations.literal: Empress Qinsheng Xiansu of Shenzong, née Xiang—on the thirteenth day of the first month in the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo she died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinsheng Xiansu of Shenzong, Lady Xiang—died on the thirteenth day of the first month in the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo.

sentences.zh: 二月，太常寺言：「大行皇太后山陵一行法物，宜依元豐二年慈聖光獻皇后故事。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "Ritual objects for the mountain mausoleum procession of the late Grand Empress Dowager should follow the precedent of Empress Cisheng Guangxian in the second year of Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Ritual objects for the late Grand Empress Dowager's mountain mausoleum procession should follow the precedent set for Empress Cisheng Guangxian in the second year of Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 皇堂之制，下深六十九尺，面方二丈五尺，石地穴深一丈，明高二丈一尺。

translations.literal: Regulations for the imperial crypt: depth below sixty-nine chi, face square two zhang five chi, stone ground pit one zhang deep, height above two zhang one chi.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial crypt was to be sixty-nine chi deep below, with a face two zhang and five chi square, a stone ground pit one zhang deep, and two zhang and one chi high above.

sentences.zh: 鵲台二，各高四丈一尺。

translations.literal: Two magpie platforms, each four zhang one chi high.
translations.idiomatic: There were two magpie platforms, each four zhang and one chi high.

sentences.zh: 乳台二，各高二丈七尺。

translations.literal: Two nursing platforms, each two zhang seven chi high.
translations.idiomatic: There were two nursing platforms, each two zhang and seven chi high.

sentences.zh: 神牆高一丈三尺。」

translations.literal: The spirit wall was one zhang three chi high."
translations.idiomatic: The spirit wall was one zhang and three chi high."

sentences.zh: 五月六日，葬永裕陵。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the fifth month, she was buried at Yongyu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the fifth month she was buried at Yongyu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，祔於神宗廟室。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day, she was enshrined in Shenzong's temple chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day she was enshrined in Shenzong's temple chamber.

sentences.zh: 哲宗皇后劉氏，政和三年二月九日崩。

translations.literal: Empress of Zhezong, née Liu—on the ninth day of the second month in the third year of Zhenghe she died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of Zhezong, Lady Liu—died on the ninth day of the second month in the third year of Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 詔：「崇恩太后合行禮儀，可依欽成皇后及開寶皇后故事，參酌裁定。」

translations.literal: Edict: "Rites to be performed for Empress Dowager Chong'en may follow the precedents of Empress Qincheng and Empress Kaibao, deliberated and fixed."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The rites for Empress Dowager Chong'en may follow the precedents of Empress Qincheng and Empress Kaibao, to be deliberated and fixed."

sentences.zh: 閏四月，上諡曰昭懷皇后。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month, the posthumous title Illustrious and Commiserating Empress was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month she received the posthumous title Illustrious and Commiserating Empress.

sentences.zh: 五月，葬永泰陵，祔神主於哲宗廟室。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, she was buried at Yongtai Mausoleum; her spirit tablet was enshrined in Zhezong's temple chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month she was buried at Yongtai Mausoleum and her spirit tablet enshrined in Zhezong's temple chamber.

sentences.zh: 徽宗皇后王氏，大觀二年九月二十六日崩。

translations.literal: Empress of Huizong, née Wang—on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month in the second year of Daguan she died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of Huizong, Lady Wang—died on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month in the second year of Daguan.

sentences.zh: 尚書省言：「章穆皇后故事，真宗服七日。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat said: "By the precedent of Empress Zhangmu, Zhenzong mourned seven days."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "By the precedent of Empress Zhangmu, Zhenzong observed seven days of mourning."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十月，太史局言：「大行皇后園陵斬草用十月二十四日斥，土用十一月十三日，葬用十二月二十七日。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Astronomy Bureau said: "For the late Empress's garden mausoleum, cutting grass on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month by divination, earth on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month, burial on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Astronomy Bureau reported: "For the late Empress's garden mausoleum, cutting the grass is set for the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month by divination, moving earth for the thirteenth day of the eleventh month, and burial for the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 諸宗室合祔葬者，並依大行皇后月日時刻。」

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen to be buried as companions—all follow the late Empress's year, month, day, and hour."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen to be buried as companion tombs should all follow the late Empress's year, month, day, and hour."

sentences.zh: 十一月，宰臣蔡京等請上諡曰靖和皇后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Chancellor Cai Jing and others requested the posthumous title Tranquil and Harmonious Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chancellor Cai Jing and others requested the posthumous title Tranquil and Harmonious Empress.

sentences.zh: 十二月，奉安梓宮於永裕陵之下宮，神主祔別廟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the spirit coffin was installed at the lower palace of Yongyu Mausoleum; the spirit tablet was enshrined in the separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the spirit coffin was installed at the lower palace of Yongyu Mausoleum and the spirit tablet enshrined in the separate temple.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，改諡曰惠恭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the posthumous title was changed to Kind and Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year her posthumous title was changed to Kind and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 其後，高宗復改曰顯恭。

translations.literal: Later, Gaozong again changed it to Illustrious and Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gaozong changed it again to Illustrious and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 徽宗顯仁皇后韋氏，紹興二十九年崩，祔於永祐陵欑宮。

translations.literal: Empress Xianren of Huizong, née Wei—in the twenty-ninth year of Shaoxing she died and was enshrined at the coffin palace of Yongyou Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xianren of Huizong, Lady Wei—died in the twenty-ninth year of Shaoxing and was enshrined at the coffin palace of Yongyou Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 高宗憲聖慈烈皇后吳氏，慶元三年崩。

translations.literal: Empress Xiansheng Cilie of Gaozong, née Wu—in the third year of Qingyuan she died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiansheng Cilie of Gaozong, Lady Wu—died in the third year of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 時光宗以太上皇承重，甯宗降服齊衰期。

translations.literal: At the time Guangzong, as retired emperor, bore the chief mourning; Ningzong wore reduced second-grade mourning for the full term.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guangzong, as retired emperor, bore the chief mourning burden, while Ningzong wore reduced second-grade mourning for the full term.

sentences.zh: 四年三月甲子，權欑於永思陵。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the third month in the fourth year, she was provisionally placed in the coffin at Yongsai Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the third month in the fourth year she was provisionally laid in the coffin at Yongsai Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 孝宗成肅皇后夏氏，開禧三年崩，殯於永阜陵正北。

translations.literal: Empress Chengsu of Xiaozong, née Xia—in the third year of Kaixi she died and was laid in state due north of Yongfu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chengsu of Xiaozong, Lady Xia—died in the third year of Kaixi and was laid in state due north of Yongfu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書陸峻言：「伏睹列聖在禦，間有諸後上仙，緣無山陵可祔，是致別葬。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Lu Jun said: "I have observed that among successive sage emperors on the throne, sometimes empresses ascended to immortality; because there was no mountain mausoleum to enshrine beside, separate burial resulted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Lu Jun memorialized: "I have observed that under successive sage emperors, some empresses passed away when no mountain mausoleum was yet available for companion burial, and so were buried separately.

sentences.zh: 若上仙在山陵已卜之後，無有不從葬者。

translations.literal: If they ascended after the mountain mausoleum had been divined, none failed to be buried as companions.
translations.idiomatic: If an empress passed away after the mountain mausoleum had already been chosen by divination, none failed to be buried as a companion tomb.

sentences.zh: 其他諸後，葬在山陵之前，神靈既安，並不遷祔。

translations.literal: Other empresses buried before the mountain mausoleum—once the spirits were settled, none were relocated for enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: Other empresses buried before the mountain mausoleum was established, once their spirits were settled, were never moved for companion enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 惟元德、章懿二後，方其葬時，名位未正，續行追冊。

translations.literal: Only the two empresses Yuande and Zhangyi—at the time of burial their titles and ranks were not yet fixed; posthumous enregistration followed later.
translations.idiomatic: Only Empresses Yuande and Zhangyi, at the time of burial, had not yet received their proper titles and ranks; posthumous enregistration came later.

sentences.zh: 其成穆皇后，孝宗登極即行追冊，改殯所為欑宮，典禮已備，與元德、章懿事體不同，所以更不遷祔。

translations.literal: As for Empress Chengmu, when Xiaozong ascended the throne he at once posthumously enregistered her, changed the place of lying in state to a coffin palace, and the rites were complete—her case differs from Yuande and Zhangyi, so she was not relocated for enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chengmu, by contrast, received posthumous enregistration as soon as Xiaozong took the throne; her place of lying in state was changed to a coffin palace and the rites were complete. Her case differs from those of Yuande and Zhangyi, which is why she was not moved for companion enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 竊稽前件典禮，祇緣喪有前後，勢所當然，其於禮意，卻無隆殺。

translations.literal: I have examined the foregoing precedents: it is only because deaths came earlier or later, as circumstance required; in ritual meaning there is no elevation or diminution.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined these precedents: differences arise only from whether death came before or after the mausoleum was fixed, as circumstance required. In ritual meaning there is no difference of greater or lesser honor.

sentences.zh: 今來從葬阜陵，為合典故。」

translations.literal: Now to be buried as a companion at Fu Mausoleum accords with precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Burial now as a companion at Fu Mausoleum accords with established precedent."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 甯宗恭聖仁烈皇后楊氏，紹定五年十二月崩，祔葬茂陵。

translations.literal: Empress Gongsheng Renlie of Ningzong, née Yang—in the twelfth month of the fifth year of Shaoding she died and was buried as a companion at Mao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gongsheng Renlie of Ningzong, Lady Yang—died in the twelfth month of the fifth year of Shaoding and was buried as a companion at Mao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 濮安懿王園廟。

translations.literal: Garden temple of Prince Pu Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: The garden temple of Prince Pu Anyi the Tranquil and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，詔置園令一人，以大使臣為之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping, an edict established one garden commissioner, to be a grand ambassador.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiping an edict established one garden commissioner, to be filled by a grand ambassador.

sentences.zh: 募兵二百人，以奉園為額。

translations.literal: Two hundred soldiers were recruited under the quota 'Serving the Garden.'
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred soldiers were recruited under the designation Serving the Garden.

sentences.zh: 置柏子戶五十人。

translations.literal: Fifty cypress-seed households were established.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty cypress-keeper households were established.

sentences.zh: 廟三間二廈，神門屋二所，及齋院、神廚、靈星門。

translations.literal: The temple had three bays and two side halls, two spirit-gate buildings, and a fasting courtyard, spirit kitchen, and Spirit Star Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The temple had three bays and two side halls, two spirit-gate buildings, and a fasting courtyard, spirit kitchen, and Spirit Star Gate.

sentences.zh: 其告祭濮安懿王及諸神祝文，並本宮教授撰。

translations.literal: Prayers for announcing sacrifices to Prince Pu Anyi and the various spirits were all composed by the instructor of that palace.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer texts for announcing sacrifices to Prince Pu Anyi and the various spirits were all composed by the palace instructor.

sentences.zh: 河南府給香幣、酒脯、禮物。

translations.literal: Henan Prefecture supplied incense, silks, wine, dried meat, and ritual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Prefecture supplied incense, silks, wine, dried meat, and ritual gifts.

sentences.zh: 太祝、奉禮則命永安縣尉、主簿攝，如闕官，以本府曹官。

translations.literal: Grand invoker and ritual attendant were assigned to the Yong'an county captain and registrar as acting officers; if offices were vacant, prefectural section officials served.
translations.idiomatic: The grand invoker and ritual attendant were assigned to the Yong'an county captain and registrar as acting officers; if posts were vacant, prefectural section officials filled them.

sentences.zh: 凡祭告及四仲饗，並依此制。

translations.literal: All announcement sacrifices and the four seasonal offerings followed this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: All announcement sacrifices and the four seasonal offerings followed this regulation.

sentences.zh: 奉安神主三獻，命西京差判官一員亞獻，朝臣一員終獻，攝。

translations.literal: For installing the spirit tablet with three offerings, one Western Capital acting judge was ordered as second offering, one court official as final offering, acting.
translations.idiomatic: For installing the spirit tablet with three offerings, one acting judge from the Western Capital was assigned as second offering and one court official as final offering, both in acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 知園令出納神主。

translations.literal: The garden commissioner received and issued the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The garden commissioner received and issued the spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 廟制用一品，夫人任氏墳域亦稱為園。

translations.literal: The temple regulations used first rank; Lady Ren's tomb domain was also called a garden.
translations.idiomatic: The temple was regulated at first rank; the tomb domain of Lady Ren was also styled a garden.

sentences.zh: 元豐詔曰：「濮安懿王，先帝斟酌典禮，即園立廟，詔王子孫歲時奉祀，義協恩稱，後世無得議焉。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng edict said: "Prince Pu Anyi—the former emperor deliberated the canonical rites, established a temple at the garden, and ordered the prince's descendants to offer seasonal sacrifice year by year; the meaning accords with title and favor; posterity may not debate it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of Yuanfeng stated: "Prince Pu Anyi—the former emperor weighed the canonical rites, established a temple at his garden, and ordered the prince's descendants to offer seasonal sacrifice every year. The arrangement accords with title and favor, and posterity may not debate it.

sentences.zh: 今三夫人名位或未正，塋域或異處，有司置而不講，曷足以彰明先帝甚盛之德，仰承在天之志乎？

translations.literal: Now the three consorts' titles and ranks may be unfixed, their tomb domains in different places; the offices set them aside without deliberation—how can this manifest the former emperor's abundant virtue or carry out the will of one in Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Now the three consorts' titles and ranks may remain unsettled and their tomb domains lie in different places, while the offices neglect the matter without deliberation. How can this manifest the former emperor's abundant virtue or carry out his will in Heaven?

sentences.zh: 三夫人可並稱曰'王夫人'，命主司擇歲月遷祔濮園，俾其子孫以時奉主與王合食，而致孝思焉。」

translations.literal: The three consorts may all be styled 'Consorts of the Prince'; order the responsible office to select the year and month to relocate and enshrine them at Pu Garden, so their descendants may in season present the lord and share food with the Prince, fulfilling filial thought."
translations.idiomatic: The three consorts may all be styled Consorts of the Prince. Let the responsible office choose the year and month to relocate and enshrine them at Pu Garden, so their descendants may in due season present the tablets and share offerings with the Prince, fulfilling filial devotion."

sentences.zh: 禮官奏請，王夫人遷葬給鹵簿全仗，用鼓吹，至國門外減半。

translations.literal: Rites officials memorialized requesting that for the consorts' relocation burial, full insignia and complete guard be granted, with drums and pipes used, halved outside the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials memorialized that the consorts' relocation burial be granted full insignia and a complete guard, with drums and pipes, halved outside the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 喪行與四時告享，並令嗣濮王主之。

translations.literal: Funeral procession and the four seasonal announcement offerings were all ordered to be presided over by the heir to Prince Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral procession and the four seasonal announcement offerings were all ordered to be presided over by the heir to Prince Pu.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，主奉祠事，以嗣濮王為之；

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, presiding over sacrificial affairs was assigned to the heir to Prince Pu;
translations.idiomatic: After the southward crossing, presiding over sacrificial affairs was assigned to the heir to Prince Pu;

sentences.zh: 園令一員，以宗室為之；

translations.literal: one garden commissioner, drawn from the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: one garden commissioner, drawn from the imperial clan;

sentences.zh: 祠堂主管兼園廟香火官一員，以武臣為之。

translations.literal: one shrine superintendent also serving as garden-temple incense officer, drawn from military officials.
translations.idiomatic: and one shrine superintendent also serving as garden-temple incense officer, drawn from military officials.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年九月，詔每歲給降福建度牒一十道，充祠堂仲饗、忌祭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Shaoxing, an edict granted ten Fujian ordination certificates each year for the shrine's mid-season and memorial-day offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Shaoxing an edict granted ten Fujian ordination certificates each year for the shrine's mid-season and memorial-day offerings.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，嗣濮王仲湜言：「被旨迎奉濮安懿王神主至行在，今已至紹興府，欲權就本處奉安。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, the heir to Prince Pu Zhongshi said: "By order I have escorted Prince Pu Anyi's spirit tablet to the mobile court; it has now reached Shaoxing Prefecture, and I wish provisionally to install it here."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year the heir to Prince Pu, Zhongshi, reported: "By imperial order I have escorted Prince Pu Anyi's spirit tablet to the mobile court. It has now reached Shaoxing Prefecture, and I ask to install it provisionally at this location."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，神主、神貌在廬州，嗣濮王士從乞奉遷於穩便州郡安奉故也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the spirit tablet and spirit likeness were in Luzhou; the heir to Prince Pu, Shicong, had requested escort and relocation to a secure prefecture for installation—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the spirit tablet and spirit likeness had been at Luzhou; the heir to Prince Pu, Shicong, had requested that they be escorted to a secure prefecture for installation.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，知大宗正事、權主奉濮安懿王祠堂土夽言：「濮安懿王神貌、神主權於紹興府光孝寺，仲享薦祭，其獻官、牲牢、禮料並多簡略。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau and acting presider over Prince Pu Anyi's shrine Tu Shen said: "Prince Pu Anyi's spirit likeness and spirit tablet are provisionally at Guangxiao Temple in Shaoxing Prefecture; mid-season offerings—the offering officials, sacrificial animals, and ritual supplies are all much simplified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Tu Shen, Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau and acting presider over Prince Pu Anyi's shrine, reported: "Prince Pu Anyi's spirit likeness and spirit tablet are provisionally at Guangxiao Temple in Shaoxing Prefecture. For mid-season offerings, the offering officials, sacrificial animals, and ritual supplies are all greatly simplified.

sentences.zh: 乞令有司討論舊制。」

translations.literal: I request that the relevant offices deliberate the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the relevant offices deliberate the former regulations."

sentences.zh: 行下禮部、太常寺令參酌，欲令土夽攝初獻，仍差士夽子或從子二人攝亞、終獻。

translations.literal: The order was transmitted to the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation, intending to have Tu Shen act as initial offering, and additionally to dispatch two of Tu Shen's sons or grandsons to act as second and final offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The order was sent down to the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation, with Tu Shen to serve as initial offering and two of his sons or grandsons assigned to act as second and final offerings.

sentences.zh: 其合用牲牢，羊、豕各一；

translations.literal: For the appropriate sacrificial victims, one sheep and one pig each;
translations.idiomatic: The appropriate sacrificial victims were one sheep and one pig;

sentences.zh: 籩、豆各十，設禮料。

translations.literal: ten each of wooden and ceramic vessels, with ritual supplies set out.
translations.idiomatic: ten each of wooden and ceramic vessels, with ritual supplies provided.

sentences.zh: 初獻合服八旒冕，亞獻、終獻合服四旒冕，奉禮郎、太祝、太官令服無旒冕，並以舊制從事。

translations.literal: The initial offering officer should wear the eight-tassel crown, the second and final offering officers the four-tassel crown; Masters of Ceremonies, Grand Invocators, and Grand Stewards should wear crownless caps—all according to the former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The initial offering officer was to wear the eight-tassel crown and the second and final offering officers the four-tassel crown; Masters of Ceremonies, Grand Invocators, and Grand Stewards were to wear crownless caps—all according to the former regulations.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 二十六年二月，嗣濮王士俴言：「濮安懿王祠堂，外無門牖，內闕龕帳，別無供具，望下紹興府置造修奉。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-sixth year, Shiqiao, heir to Prince Pu, said: "Prince Pu Anyi's ancestral hall has no doors or windows on the exterior, lacks niches and curtains within, and has no offerings equipment. I ask that orders be sent to Shaoxing Prefecture to commission and maintain it."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-sixth year Shiqiao, heir to Prince Pu, reported: "Prince Pu Anyi's ancestral hall has no doors or windows on the outside, lacks niches and curtains within, and has no offering equipment. I ask that Shaoxing Prefecture be ordered to commission and maintain it.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年四月詔：「濮安懿王祠堂園廟，自今實及三年，令本堂牒紹興府檢計修葺。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Chunxi, an edict stated: "For Prince Pu Anyi's ancestral hall and garden temple, from now every third year the office shall dispatch a memorial to Shaoxing Prefecture to inspect and repair."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Chunxi an edict stated: "For Prince Pu Anyi's ancestral hall and garden temple, from now every third year the office shall notify Shaoxing Prefecture to inspect and repair the site.

sentences.zh: 從嗣濮王士輵請也。

translations.literal: This followed a request from Shige, heir to Prince Pu.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a request from Shige, heir to Prince Pu.

sentences.zh: 秀安僖王園廟。

translations.literal: Garden temple of Prince Xiu Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: The garden temple of Prince Xiu Anxi the Secure and Deferential.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年三月，詔秀王襲封等典禮。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Shaoxi, an edict [established] the rituals for Prince Xiu's succession and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Shaoxi an edict established the rituals for Prince Xiu's succession and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 禮部、太堂寺乞依濮安懿王典禮，避秀安僖王名一字。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested following Prince Pu Anyi's rituals, tabooing one character of Prince Xiu Anxi's name.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices asked to follow Prince Pu Anyi's rituals, tabooing one character of Prince Xiu Anxi's name.

sentences.zh: 詔恭依，仍置園廟。

translations.literal: An edict approved respectfully, and a garden temple was additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request respectfully and additionally ordered a garden temple established.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔：「皇伯滎陽郡王伯圭除太保，依前安德軍節度使，充萬壽觀使，嗣秀王，以奉王祀。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month, an edict stated: "Imperial uncle, Prince of Fuyang Commandery Bogui is appointed Grand Guardian, continuing as military commissioner of Ande Army as before, serving as commissioner of Wanshou Palace, succeeding as Prince Xiu to perform the prince's sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict stated: "Imperial uncle Bogui, Prince of Fuyang Commandery, is appointed Grand Guardian, continues as military commissioner of Ande Army as before, serves as commissioner of Wanshou Palace, succeeds as Prince Xiu, and is charged with performing the prince's sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 六月，禮部、太常寺言：「濮安懿王園廟制度，廟堂、神門宜並用獸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "For Prince Pu Anyi's garden temple regulations, the temple hall and spirit gate should both employ beast-ridge ornamentation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Under Prince Pu Anyi's garden temple regulations, the temple hall and spirit gate should both employ beast-ridge ornamentation.

sentences.zh: 所安木主石塪，於室中西壁三分之一近南去地四尺開坎室，以石為之，其中可容神主趺匱。

translations.literal: For the wooden spirit tablet stone niche: in the chamber, on the west wall at one-third from the south, four chi above ground, excavate a niche chamber made of stone, within which can hold the spirit tablet pedestal and case.
translations.idiomatic: For the wooden spirit tablet stone niche: in the chamber, on the west wall one-third from the south and four chi above the ground, a stone niche chamber is to be opened, large enough to hold the spirit tablet pedestal and case.

sentences.zh: 今來秀安僖王及夫人神主，欲乞並依上件典禮。

translations.literal: For Prince Xiu Anxi and his consort's spirit tablets, we request that both follow the above regulations.
translations.idiomatic: For the spirit tablets of Prince Xiu Anxi and his consort, we ask that both follow the regulations above.

sentences.zh: 四仲饗廟，三獻官並奉禮郎等，系嗣秀王充初獻，本位侄男攝亞、終獻，其奉禮郎等，乞湖州差官充攝。

translations.literal: For the four seasonal temple offerings, the three offering officers and Masters of Ceremonies etc.: the successor Prince Xiu should serve as initial offering; sons and nephews of his rank should act as second and final offerings; for the Masters of Ceremonies etc., we ask that Huzhou dispatch officials to serve in acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: For the four seasonal temple offerings, the three offering officers and Masters of Ceremonies: the successor Prince Xiu should serve as initial offering, sons and nephews of his rank should act as second and final offerings, and we ask that Huzhou dispatch officials to serve as acting Masters of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 行禮合用牲羊、豕，湖州排辦；

translations.literal: For the ritual, the appropriate sacrificial sheep and pigs should be arranged by Huzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The sheep and pigs required for the ritual were to be arranged by Huzhou;

sentences.zh: 祭器、祭服，工部下文思院製造。

translations.literal: Sacrificial vessels and robes: the Ministry of Works should order the Wensi Institute to manufacture them.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial vessels and robes were to be manufactured by the Wensi Institute on orders from the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 每遇仲饗，本府前期牒報湖州排辦。

translations.literal: Whenever a seasonal offering occurred, this prefecture should in advance dispatch a memorial notifying Huzhou to arrange matters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a seasonal offering occurred, this prefecture was to notify Huzhou in advance to make the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 所有行禮儀注，乞從太堂寺參照濮安懿王儀注修定。」

translations.literal: For all ritual protocols, we ask that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices consult Prince Pu Anyi's protocols and revise them accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: For all ritual protocols, we ask that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices consult Prince Pu Anyi's protocols and revise them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved.

sentences.zh: 其園廟差禦帶霍漢臣同湖州通判一員相度聞奏。

translations.literal: For the garden temple, Imperial Guard-with-Belt Huo Hanchen was dispatched together with one Huzhou vice-prefect to survey and report.
translations.idiomatic: For the garden temple, Imperial Guard-with-Belt Huo Hanchen was dispatched together with one vice-prefect of Huzhou to survey the site and report.

sentences.zh: 八月，霍漢臣暨通判湖州朱僎言奉詔相度園廟，以圖來上。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Huo Hanchen and Zhu Suan, vice-prefect of Huzhou, reported that per edict they had surveyed the garden temple and submitted a plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Huo Hanchen and Zhu Suan, vice-prefect of Huzhou, reported that by edict they had surveyed the garden temple and submitted a plan.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔委通判一員，提督修造祠堂，如法修蓋。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict assigned one vice-prefect to supervise repair and construction of the ancestral hall, repairing and roofing according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict assigned one vice-prefect to supervise repair and construction of the ancestral hall, with roofing and repairs to be carried out according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 十一月，禮工部、太常寺言：「濮安懿王園廟三間二廈、神門屋二坐、齋院、神廚、靈星門，欲令湖州照應建造。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Ministries of Rites and Works and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Prince Pu Anyi's garden temple—three bays and two side halls, two spirit-gate buildings, a fasting courtyard, spirit kitchen, and Spirit Star Gate—we ask that Huzhou be ordered to construct correspondingly."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Ministries of Rites and Works and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Prince Pu Anyi's garden temple has three bays and two side halls, two spirit-gate buildings, a fasting courtyard, a spirit kitchen, and a Spirit Star Gate. We ask that Huzhou be ordered to build accordingly.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 三年正月一收，嗣秀王伯圭奏：「建造秀安僖王園廟，近已畢工，所有修制神主儀式，令所司檢照典故修制，委官題寫。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, heir Prince Xiu Bogui memorialized: "Construction of Prince Xiu Anxi's garden temple has recently been completed. For the protocols for making the spirit tablets, let the relevant offices consult precedents and commission officials to inscribe them."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Bogui, heir Prince Xiu, memorialized: "Construction of Prince Xiu Anxi's garden temple has recently been completed. For the protocols for making the spirit tablets, let the relevant offices consult precedents, prepare them accordingly, and commission officials to inscribe them.

sentences.zh: 詔差權禮部尚書李巘題寫。

translations.literal: An edict assigned Acting Minister of Rites Li Yan to inscribe them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict assigned Acting Minister of Rites Li Yan to inscribe them.

sentences.zh: 二月，伯圭又奏：「秀安僖王祠堂園廟，乞從濮安懿王例，每三年一次，從本所移牒所屬州府檢計修造。」

translations.literal: In the second month, Bogui again memorialized: "For Prince Xiu Anxi's ancestral hall and garden temple, I ask that following Prince Pu Anyi's precedent, every three years this office dispatch a memorial to the subordinate prefecture to inspect and repair."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Bogui again memorialized: "For Prince Xiu Anxi's ancestral hall and garden temple, I ask that following Prince Pu Anyi's precedent, every three years this office notify the responsible prefecture to inspect and repair the site.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 莊文太子喪禮。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for Crown Prince Zhuang Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for Crown Prince Zhuang Wen.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年七月九日，皇太子薨。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the seventh month of the third year of Qiandao, the Crown Prince died.
